title: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways successfully concludes Special Campaign 6 for institutionalising Swachhata and reducing pendency
subtitle: Campaign achieves over 100% of targets under various parameters; cleanliness and sanitation activities undertaken at more than 4,960 locations
body_text: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and its agencies have successfully concluded the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters (SCDPM) 6, conducted from 2nd to 31st October, 2026. This year, Ministry under cleanliness drive, included repair work of NH providing swachh roads to public and enhancing user experience.  As reported by the field formations, more than 95,000 km of National Highways and service roads were made pothole-free, while road signage and road markings were improved along stretches covering more than 65,000 km. Further, approximately 5,000 functional toilets were cleaned and more than 500 toilets at toll plazas were refurbished. Plantation activities along the central verges of National Highways were also undertaken across stretches covering more than 7,000 km. During the Campaign, the Ministry achieved more than 100% of the targets set under various parameters, including disposal of Public Grievances (5,960), Public Grievance Appeals (1,013), IMC References (3) and Record Management (review of 14,625 old physical files/e-files). Further, the Ministry disposed of 304 pending MP References and 77 State Government References. In addition, 4 Parliamentary Assurances and 17 PMO references were also disposed of during the Campaign. MoRTH and its agencies undertook extensive cleanliness and sanitation activities at more than 4,960 locations, including offices, construction camps/sites, National Highway stretches, Toll Plazas, Wayside Amenities, roadside dhabas, bus stops, flyovers, etc. Space management and beautification activities were also undertaken at various office premises. Further, more than 1134 kg of scrap, including e-waste was disposed of, generating revenue amounting to Rs.1,20,100/- The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways also undertook various cleanliness, maintenance and improvement activities related to its core functions in a coordinated manner under the Swachhata Hi Seva Campaign (17 September 2026 to 2 October 2026) and Special Campaign 6 (2 October 2026 to 31 October 2026), with the objective of ensuring cleanliness and proper upkeep of National Highways. To ensure the achievement of targets identified under various parameters of the Campaign, the Secretary, MoRTH, reviewed the progress on a weekly basis. Further, the Nodal Officer of the Campaign in the Ministry regularly coordinated with and followed up with all concerned agencies to ensure the timely achievement of targets. The successful implementation of Special Campaign 6 reflects the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways’ continued commitment to promoting cleanliness, improving administrative efficiency, strengthening accountability and creating a productive work environment. *** GDH/DS/HJ
